issues.description: The template's Main.java shows example instantiation of Seal, Pig, and Goat using two-argument constructors (e.g., new Seal("Clarabelle", "marine")), while the problem specification and the solution implement these animal constructors with a single parameter (name) only. This mismatch in constructor parameters can confuse students about the required constructors and may lead to compilation errors if they rely on the example in the template.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template's example usage consistent with the specification: update template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java to instantiate animals with a single String name argument (e.g., new Seal("Clarabelle")). Alternatively, if two-argument constructors are intended, update the problem statement and solution to document and implement the additional parameter across the Animal subclasses.

issues.description: The template's commented example code instantiates animals using two-argument constructors (e.g., Seal("Clarabelle", "marine")), whereas the UML in the problem statement and the solution repository use single-argument constructors that accept only the name. This mismatch between the template example and the stated/implemented class design can confuse students about the required class attributes and constructor signatures.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template example consistent with the UML and solution by using single-argument constructors that only take the animal name (e.g., Seal("Clarabelle"), Pig("Doodle"), Goat("Buttinsky")). If a second attribute was intended, instead update the UML, problem text, and solution to include and name that attribute consistently across all artifacts.
